rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form with a doubled dāl and fatḥa on bāʾ conveys intensification; both it and the ungeminated form are good and have been read.
rows.anchor: وقرئت (يبدله)، بتشديد الدال وفتح الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes gloss qānitāt as obedient; linguistically, qunūt is carrying out acts that bring one near to God.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير مطيعات، والقنوت القيام بما يقرب إلى الله

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic interpretation says that the male and female sāʾiḥūn are those who fast; the source adds that this interpretation occurs in earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أن السائحين هم الصائمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Linguists explain the name for a faster by comparison with a worshipping traveler who carries no provisions and eats when food becomes available.
rows.anchor: قال أهل اللغة: إنما قيل للصائم سائح لأن الذي يسيح متعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Protect yourselves and your families by doing what draws you near to God and keeping yourselves and them away from sins.
rows.anchor: خذوا أنفسكم وأهليكم بما يقرب من الله - جل وعز -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An exegetical exhortation urges a man to attend to his family's prayer, fasting, and care for the poor, orphan, and neighbors; this means maintaining these duties and fulfilling God's obligations in them.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير: رحم الله رجلا قال: يا أهلاه صلاتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says that God may gather the family together with the man in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث لعل الله يجمعهم معه في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes identify the stones that fuel the fire as sulfur stones.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أنها حجارة الكبريت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa on wāw, waqūd means the material used to kindle a fire, such as firewood; with ḍamma, wuqūd names the fire's burning.
rows.anchor: والوقود بفتح الواو ما توقد به النار من حطب وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is read with fatḥa or ḍamma on the nūn; the fatḥa reading makes it an adjective of repentance, while the ḍamma reading means they counsel sincerely.
rows.anchor: بفتح النون، وتقرأ (نصوحا) - بضم النون - فمن فتح فعلى صفة التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the fatḥa reading, naṣūḥ describes repentance as fully sincere; fuʿūl can intensify an active quality, as in ṣabūr and shakūr.
rows.anchor: ومعناه توبة بالغة في النصح، وفعول من أسماء الفاعلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the ḍamma reading, the phrase means that they counsel with sincere counsel; Arabic also uses naṣaḥa lahu, naṣāḥatan, and naṣūḥan.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ (نصوحا) - بضم النون - فمعناه ينصحون بهذا نصوحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One exegetical definition calls sincere repentance repentance after which the penitent does not return to sin.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن التوبة النصوح التي لا يعاود التائب معها المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another definition is repentance in which the penitent does not intend to return to sin.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم التي لا ينوي معها معاودة المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening is read either by assimilating nūn into wāw, by articulating the nūn distinctly before wāw, or as Nūn with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: قرئت بإدغام النون في الواو، وقرئت بتبيين النون عند الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjāj prefers assimilation into wāw whether wāw is still or vowelled, since the exegetical accounts distinguish the opening from a bare letter-name; assimilation can occur with nūn open.
rows.anchor: والذي اختار إدغام النون في الواو كانت الواو ساكنة أو متحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One exegetical account identifies Nūn as the fish on which the seven earths were spread.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن " نون " الحوت التي دحيت عليها سبع الأرضين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another exegetical account identifies nūn as an inkpot; the source says the accounts do not interpret it as one of the alphabetic letter names.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أيضا أن النون الدواة، ولم يجئ في التفسير كما فسرت حروف الهجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A vowelless nūn is possible only if it is treated as a letter name, which is why that reading does not fit the other exegetical interpretations.
rows.anchor: والإسكان لا يجوز أن يكون فيه إلا حرف هجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Pen was the first creation; God commanded it to write the decree, and it recorded what would happen until the Resurrection, including the fate of Abū Lahab.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن أول ما خلق الله القلم، فقال له: اكتب، فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is written refers to what the angels write.
rows.anchor: وقوله: (وما يسطرون). معناه: وما تكتب الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the construction with mā, anta is its subject and bi-majnūn its predicate; bi-niʿmati rabbika is attached to the negation.
rows.anchor: قوله: (أنت) هو اسم (ما)، و (بمجنون) الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sense is that, by your Lord's grace, madness is absent from you, just as one may say that God's blessing made someone understanding rather than ignorant.
rows.anchor: المعنى: انتفى عنك الجنون بنعمة ربك، كما تقول: أنت بنعمة الله فهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This denial answers the opponents' claim that the recipient of the Reminder was mad.
rows.anchor: وهذا جواب لقولهم: (وقالوا يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unending reward is one that is not cut off; exegetes also gloss the phrase as unreckoned.
rows.anchor: أي: غير مقطوع، وجاء في التفسير: غير محسوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two reported interpretations gloss the great character as Islam or as the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: قيل: على الإسلام، وقيل: على القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjāj's preferred explanation is that the Prophet follows the character God commanded in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: والمعنى - والله أعلم - أنت على الخلق الذي أمرك الله به في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents wished the Prophet would compromise with them in religion so they would compromise with him in return.
rows.anchor: أي: ودوا لو تصانعهم في الدين فيصانعونك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mahīn derives from lowliness or smallness; here it means deficient in judgment and discernment.
rows.anchor: ومعناه ههنا القلة في الرأي والتمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hammāz is someone who backbites people.
rows.anchor: الهماز الذي يغتاب الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person described kept his family, children, and close kin from accepting Islam.
rows.anchor: معناه: كان يمنع أهله وولده ولحمته من الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes identify him as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī, a wealthy man with ten sons who threatened to withhold support from any son or kinsman who became Muslim.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أنه الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي، وكان موسرا كثير المال، وكان له عشرة بنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Walīd's reported threat was that he would cut off his support from whoever among his sons or close kin accepted Islam.
rows.anchor: من أسلم منكم منعته رفدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A transgressor is one who goes beyond bounds in oppression; athīm means sinful toward his Lord through transgression and wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: أي متجاوز في الظلم، وأثيم: أي أثيم بربه، أي أثيم باعتدائه وذنبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes gloss ʿutull as fiercely contentious; another gloss is harsh in character and base in disposition.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن العتل ههنا الشديد الخصومة، وجاء في التفسير أنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, ʿutull means coarse and harsh.
rows.anchor: وهو في اللغة الغليظ الجافي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One Arabic explanation is someone attached to a tribe despite not belonging to it; Ḥassān ibn Thābit's verse uses zanīm of someone attached to the Hāshim clan.
rows.anchor: قال حسان بن ثابت الأنصاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is a person notorious for evil, like a goat recognized by the dangling appendage at its throat.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الزنيم الذي يعرف بالشر كما تعرف الشاة بزنمتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zaʿīm means guarantor or surety; the question asks which of them guaranteed the claim.
rows.anchor: والزعيم الكفيل والضامن. والمعنى سلهم أيهم كفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge is for them to bring their alleged partners on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي فليأتوا بشركائهم يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, uncovering a shin is an idiom for the disclosure of a grave or severe matter; the cited battle verse illustrates the idiom.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (يكشف عن ساق) في اللغة يكشف عن الأمر الشديد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the phrase as the disclosure of a severe matter.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في قوله: (يكشف عن ساق) عن الأمر الشديد

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that the Merciful will uncover His shin: believers will prostrate to Him, while hypocrites' backs will become rigid, vertebra after vertebra, like skewers.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: يكشف الرحمن عن ساقه. فأما المؤمنون فيخرون له سجدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjāj takes the inability to prostrate and the following description of humbled eyes to refer to the hypocrites.
rows.anchor: هذا تأويل قوله (ويدعون إلى السجود فلا يستطيعون (42) خاشعة أبصارهم). يعني به المنافقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their humiliation will cover them.
rows.anchor: (ترهقهم ذلة) معناه تغشاهم ذلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were called to prostrate while they were still sound and safe in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود وهم سالمون (43) يعني به في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means not to occupy one's heart with the denier: leave his case to God, who will requite him.
rows.anchor: معناه لا تشغل قلبك به، كله إلي فإني أجازيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom ذرني وإياه does not mean restrain him; it means leave his affair to me and I will take care of it.
rows.anchor: ومثله قول الرجل: ذرني وإياه. وليس أنه منعه به ولكن تأويله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion of the fish is Jonah.
rows.anchor: يعني: يونس عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makẓūm means filled with grief and distress.
rows.anchor: أي مملوء غما وكربا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah was cast into the open place but was not blameworthy, as God's favor had encompassed him.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنه قد نبذ بالعراء وهو غير مذموم، ويدل على ذلك أن النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind was extremely cold; ṣarṣar denotes intense cold, and the source discusses whether the doubled form conveys repetition.
rows.anchor: أي بريح شديدة البرد جدا، والصرصر شدة البرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjāj compares ṣarṣar with doubled and undoubled Arabic forms: qalqala entails repeated lifting whereas aqalla means lifting, and doubled sound forms such as ṣarṣar or ṣalṣal contrast with ṣar or ṣal.
rows.anchor: إلا أن قلقلته رددته أي كررت رفعه، وأقللته رفعته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind was kept over them as God willed.
rows.anchor: معنى (سخرها عليهم) أقامها عليهم كما شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is glossed as lasting; another gloss is successive. Zajjāj says the language instead yields the sense of cutting them off and destroying them.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (حسوما) دائمة. وقالوا متابعة، فأما ما توجبه اللغة فعلى معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb حسمهم here means that the wind eradicated and destroyed them.
rows.anchor: أي تذهبهم وتفنيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿjāz al-nakhl means palm-tree trunks or bases.
rows.anchor: (أعجاز نخل) أصول نخل، وقيل خاوية للنخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khawiya is feminine because nakhl can be treated as either masculine or feminine in Arabic.
rows.anchor: وقيل خاوية للنخل لأن النخل تذكر وتؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjāj points to another Qur'anic description of palm trunks as munqaʿir.
rows.anchor: وقال في موضع آخر: (أعجاز نخل منقعر).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase has two readings: one means his followers or adherents, while the other means those who preceded him.
rows.anchor: وقرئت ومن قبله فمن قال: ومن قبله فمعناه وتباعة، ومن قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The overturned peoples were destroyed for their sins, especially the great falsehood of disbelief and denying the messengers; their name evokes the overturning of truth into falsehood.
rows.anchor: (والمؤتفكات) الذين ائتفكوا بذنوبهم، أي أهلكوا بذنوبهم التي أعظمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-khāṭiʾa means a grave error; the following verse's account of disobeying the messenger supports the emphasis on their grave sins and denial.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (بالخاطئة) بالخطأ العظيم، والدليل على أن من عظيم آثامهم الكذب قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their disobedience included denying their messengers.
rows.anchor: قوله: (فعصوا رسول ربهم فأخذهم أخذة رابية (10) لإأنهم كذبوا رسلهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rābiya describes a seizure or punishment that exceeds other afflictions.
rows.anchor: (أخذة رابية): معنى (رابية) تزيد على الأحداث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water overflowed and rose.
rows.anchor: معنى طغى الماء طما وارتفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vessel called al-jāriya is Noah's ship.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الجارية، أي سفينة نوح عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun refers to this event: the drowning of Noah's people and the rescue of Noah and the believers with him.
rows.anchor: معناه لنجعل هذه الفعلة لكم تذكرة، أي إغراق قوم نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A receptive ear preserves what it hears and acts upon it; Arabic uses waʿaytu for retaining something inwardly but awʿaytu for putting an object into a container.
rows.anchor: معناه أذن تحفظ ما سمعت وتعمل به، أي ليحفظ السامع ما سمع ويعمل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic contrasts retaining knowledge or speech with storing belongings in a vessel: one says waʿaytu knowledge, but awʿaytu goods in a container.
rows.anchor: تقول لكل شيء حفظته في نفسك: قد وعيته، يقال: قد وعيت العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The received reading has nominative nafkhatu, construed as a passive construction; al-Akhfash also mentions the accusative nafkhatan without saying whether it was transmitted as a reading.
rows.anchor: القراءة بالرفع في (نفخة) على ما لم يسم فاعله. وذكر الأخفش (نفخة واحدة) بالنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative is grammatically possible if the phrase fī al-ṣūr stands in place of the passive agent, with the sense that the trumpet is blown once.
rows.anchor: وهي في العربية جائزة على أن قولك في الصور يقوم مقام ما لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With nominative nafkhatu, the sense is that one blast is blown in the trumpet.
rows.anchor: ومن رفع فعلى معنى نفخ نفخة واحدة في الصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb may be masculine even where feminine nafkhatan is used, since the feminine is non-natural and nafkha and nafkh carry the same meaning.
rows.anchor: فتذكيره جائز، لأن النفخة والنفخ بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source compares this non-natural feminine usage with the Qur'anic construction man jāʾahu mawʿiẓa and cites another verse with mawʿiẓa as feminine.
rows.anchor: ومثله (فمن جاءه موعظة من ربه). المعنى معنى الوعظ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to patient endurance indicates that this passage preceded the command to fight.
rows.anchor: هذا يدل على أن ذلك قبل أن يؤمر النبي عليه السلام بالقتال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents consider the promised event impossible, as in an argument that something is too far off to happen; God says it is near.
rows.anchor: يرونه بعيدا عندهم كأنهم يستبعدونه على جهة الإحالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's judgment that it is near is true: the arguments for resurrection make it readily understandable, including the argument that the one who originated life can restore it.
rows.anchor: أي صحيحا يقرب فهم مثله بما دل الله على يوم البعث بقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhl is the dregs of oil.
rows.anchor: العهن الصوف، والمهل دردي الزيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIhn means wool.
rows.anchor: العهن الصوف، والمهل دردي الزيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading omits the second ḥamīman, while another includes it; their different syntax yields different interpretations.
rows.anchor: وقرئت (ولا يسأل حميم). فمن قرأ (ولا يسأل) فالمعنى أنهم يعرف بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without the second ḥamīm, the meaning is that close associates recognize one another, supported by the statement that they see one another.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأ (ولا يسأل) فالمعنى أنهم يعرف بعضهم بعضا، ويدل عليه قوله: (يبصرونهم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the second ḥamīm, the meaning is that no relative asks about a relative; Zajjāj suggests that the ones being seen are angels.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ (ولا يسأل حميم حميما). فالمعنى لا يسأل قريب عن قرابته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faṣīla is a person's closest clan or tribe.
rows.anchor: معناه أدنى قبيلته منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā is a rebuke and an alert, meaning that none of these people will return, so take heed.
rows.anchor: (كلا) ردع وتنبيه، أي لا يرجع أحد من هؤلاء فاعتبروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage names the Fire as laẓā.
rows.anchor: كلا إنها لظى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is read in the nominative or accusative. The nominative is the readers' more common reading and is stronger grammatically; Abū ʿUbayd allows the accusative but says he knows no reader who used it.
rows.anchor: والقراءة (نزاعة)، والقراء عليها وهي في النحو أقوى من النصب.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The accusative reading is reported from al-Ḥasan; transmission from ʿĀṣim differs, with Abū ʿAmr reporting the accusative and others reporting the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقد رويت عن الحسن، واختلف فيها عن عاصم، فأما ما رواه أبو عمرو عن عاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One nominative analysis makes laẓā and nazzāʿa predicates of an implicit matter-pronoun, like saying something is both sweet and sour.
rows.anchor: أحدها أن تكون " لظى، و " نزاعة " خبرا عن الهاء والألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another nominative analysis treats nazzāʿa as a predicate of an implicit huwa, used as a blame construction.
rows.anchor: والوجه الثالث في الرفع يرفع على الذم بإضمار هي على معنى هي نزاعة للشوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative can be an emphatic circumstantial accusative, as in huwa al-ḥaqqu muṣaddiqan.
rows.anchor: فعلى أنها حال مؤكدة كما قال: (وهو الحق مصدقا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the accusative means that the Fire blazes as it tears away the extremities; it can also be accusative for blame, giving three possible accusative analyses.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن ينصب على معنى أنها تتلظى (نزاعة) كما قال جل ثناؤه:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shawā means the extremities—hands, feet, and head—and is the plural of shawāh, the skin of the head; the cited verse attests the form.
rows.anchor: والشوى الأطراف، اليدان والرجلان والرأس، والشوى جمع شواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poetic line by the poet identified in the text as Qutayla uses shawātuhu of a head covered with gray hair, witnessing the word's use.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
قالت قتيلة ما له. . . قد جللت شيبا شواته؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is read with wāw as awḥiya or without wāw as aḥiya; the latter derives from waḥaytu ilayhi, while awḥaytu is more common.
rows.anchor: القراءة (أوحي) بإثبات الواو. - قد قرئت: (قل أحي إلي) - بغير واو.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The underlying form is waḥy; wāw with ḍamma may be replaced by hamza, as in ūqqitat from waqt.
rows.anchor: والأصل وحي، ولكن الواو إذا انضمت قد تبدل منها الهمزة نحو: (وإذا الرسل أقتت)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An exegetical account says the jinn heard the Prophet reciting the dawn prayer at Baṭn Nakhlah; it connects this with the passage saying they were turned toward him and listened.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن هؤلاء النفر الذين من الجن استمعوا إلى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they arrived, some told the others to stop talking and listen.
rows.anchor: أي قال بعضهم لبعض أمسكوا عن الكلام واستمعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported identifications differ: some say the jinn came from Naṣībīn and others say Yemen.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنهم كانوا من جن نصيبين، وقيل إنهم كانوا من اليمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports disagree about their religion, identifying them either as Jews or as polytheists.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنهم كانوا يهودا، وقيل إنهم كانوا مشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle an in the clause anna istamaʿa is only read with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: فأما قوله: (أنه استمع نفر من الجن)، و (أن) مفتوحة لا غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particles in innā samiʿnā, fa-inna lahu, and fa-innahu yasluk are all read with kasra.
rows.anchor: وقوله: (إنا سمعنا) وقوله: (فإن له)، وقوله: (فإنه يسلك). فهذه الثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining ann clauses in the sūra have variant readings; Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh transmitted from ʿĀṣim like Nāfiʿ, while Ḥafṣ transmitted a kasra where Abū Bakr read a fatḥa.
rows.anchor: فأما عاصم فروى عنه أبوبكر بن عياش مثل قراءة نافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians prefer Nāfiʿ and his followers: clauses presented as revelation take fatḥa on anna, while the jinn's own statements take kasra, coordinated with their words innā samiʿnā.
rows.anchor: والذي يختاره النحويون قراءة نافع ومن تابعه في هذه الآية عندهم ما كان محمولا على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians attach the fatḥa construction to the preceding genitive pronoun, but Zajjāj calls that poor analogy because a genitive pronoun should not be coordinated without repeating its preposition.
rows.anchor: ومن فتح فذكر بعض النحويين أنه معطوف على الهاء. المعنى عنده فآمنا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fatḥa can instead be understood through the sense of āmannā bihi: the meaning is that they believed and affirmed that their Lord's majesty is exalted.
rows.anchor: ولكن وجهه أن يكون محمولا على معنى آمنا به، لأن معنى آمنا به صدقناه وعلمناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jadd here means the glory and greatness of the Lord, exalted above taking a consort or child.
rows.anchor: وتأويل (تعالى جد ربنا) تعالى جلال ربنا وعظمته عن أن يتخذ صاحبة أو ولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that God tests them by it.
rows.anchor: لنختبرهم بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣaʿad is glossed as a difficult punishment; an alternative says it is a rock in Hell, but Zajjāj favors the linguistic sense of a hard path of punishment.
rows.anchor: معناه - والله أعلم - عذابا شاقا، وقيل صخرة في جهنم - وهي في اللغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression describes a difficult, uneven route; Arabic says people are in ṣuʿūd and hubūṭ when the path is not level.
rows.anchor: يقال: قد وقع القوم في صعود وهبوط، إذا كانوا في غير استواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The neighboring verse is read la-asqaynāhum māʾan ghadaqan; ghadaq is the verbal noun and ghadiq is the active form for abundant dew or water.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ (لأسقيناهم ماء غدقا)، والغدق المصدر، والغدق اسم الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic says ghadiqa yaghdaqu when dew or water becomes abundant in a place.
rows.anchor: تقول: غدق يغدق غدقا فهو غدق، إذا كثر الندى في المكان أو الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to worship God alone in the prayers.
rows.anchor: معناه الأمر بتوحيد الله في الصلوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes al-masājid as the human body's prostration points: forehead, nose, hands, knees, and feet.
rows.anchor: وقيل المساجد مواضع السجود من الإنسان، الجبهة والأنف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause introduced by an can be accusative or genitive: it means because the mosques belong to God, with an omitted lām yielding the accusative, or genitive by Arab usage without an expressed lām.
rows.anchor: و" أن " ههنا يصلح أن يكون في موضع نصب ويصلح أن يكون في موضع جر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted-preposition genitive has an Arabic parallel in the expression wa-baladin laysa bihi anīs, meaning rubba balad.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون جرا وإن لم تظهر اللام، كما تقول العرب: وبلد ليس به أنيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word lubadan has more than one reading, with the source distinguishing vocalized forms that are represented alike in its unvowelled text.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ (لبدا)، ويجوز (لبدا).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes the subject as the jinn: after hearing and marveling at the Qur'an during the Prophet's dawn prayer at Dhāt Nakhlah, they nearly fell upon him.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - لما صلى الصبح بذات نخلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the subject as the opposing host who had banded together against the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقيل كادوا يعني به جميع الملأ التي تظاهرت على النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lubad describes things piled tightly on one another; the root also gives the name of the densely felted rugs.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (لبدا) يركب بعضه بعضا، وكل شيء ألصقته بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is parsed as a plural of libda or libd; another is treated as a plural of forms such as libda and libda, which the source says share a sense.
rows.anchor: فأما من قرأ لبدا فهو جمع لبدة ولبد. ومن قرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further analysis makes lubad a plural of lābid, on the pattern of rākiʿ to rakaʿ and ghāzin to ghuzā.
rows.anchor: ومعنى من قرأ (لبدا) فهو جمع لابد ولبد، مثل راكع وركع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Multaḥad means a place of refuge, derived from laḥd and comparable to a place of shelter, cave, or entrance.
rows.anchor: أي، منجى إلا أن اشتقاقه من اللحد، وهو مثل (لو يجدون ملجأ أو مغارات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illā balāghan is accusative as an exception replacing multaḥadan: no refuge saves him except conveying God's message.
rows.anchor: ونصب (إلا بلاغا) على البدل من قوله (ملتحدا).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nāqūr is the trumpet; an exegetical account specifies that it is the first blast.
rows.anchor: الناقور الصور، وقيل في التفسير إنه يعني به النفخة الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm ʿasīr is raised by fa-dhālika; the sense is that it is a difficult day when the trumpet is blown.
rows.anchor: (يوم عسير) يرتفع بقوله: (فذلك يومئذ). المعنى فذلك يوم عسير يوم ينفخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm idh can be nominative, built on fatḥ because it is annexed to the indeclinable idh, or accusative with the sense 'on that day'.
rows.anchor: و" يومئذ: يجوز أن يكون رفعا، ويجوز أن يكون نصبا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjāj refers readers to his earlier explanation of dharnī in Sūrat al-Muzzammil.
rows.anchor: قد فسرنا معنى (ذرني) في المزمل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waḥīdan is an accusative circumstantial phrase and has two possible referents.
rows.anchor: و (وحيدا) منصوب على الحال، وهو على وجهين:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis describes God as alone in creating the man, with no partner sharing in creation.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أن يكون وحيدا من صفة الله - عز وجل - المعنى ذرني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, waḥīdan describes the created man as having been made alone, without wealth or children.
rows.anchor: ويكون (وحيدا) من صفة المخلوق، ويكون المعنى، ذرني ومن خلقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wealth is described as continuing without interruption; another report specifies one thousand dinars.
rows.anchor: تقديره مال غير منقطع عنه، وقيل ألف دينار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His sons were present with him, so they did not need to travel away on errands.
rows.anchor: وبنين شهودا، أي شهود معه لا يحتاجون إلى أن يتصرفوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage is said to refer to al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who had ten sons and was wealthy.
rows.anchor: وهذا قيل يعنى به الوليد بن المغيرة، كان له بنون عشرة وكان موسرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The anomalous form tisʿata aʿshar is analyzed as though it were a plural pattern, comparable to yamīn and ayman.
rows.anchor: " تسعة أعشر "، وهي شاذة، كأنها على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The number of the guardians is a test for the unbelievers, some of whom say that some of them would suffice to deal with those guardians.
rows.anchor: (وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا فتنة للذين كفروا). أي محنة، لأن بعضهم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book become certain because what the Prophet brought agrees with what is in their scriptures.
rows.anchor: أي يعلمون أن ما أتى به النبي عليه السلام موافقا لما في كتبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers increase in faith whenever they affirm what comes in God's Book.
rows.anchor: لأنهم كلما صدقوا بما يأتي في كتاب الله عز وجل زاد إيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that the People of the Book and believers will not doubt.
rows.anchor: أي لا يشكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that a person keeps putting off repentance and continues committing bad deeds.
rows.anchor: معناه أنه يسوف بالتوبة، ويقدم الأعمال السيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means that a person denies what lies ahead, namely the Resurrection; the question about when the Day will be supports this reading.
rows.anchor: ويجوز - والله أعلم - أن يكون معناه ليكفر بما قدامه. ودليل ذلك قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two readings of bariqa/bariqa differ in meaning: one is panic and bewilderment, the other comes from the eye's gleam.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ (برق البصر). فمن قرأ (برق) فمعناه فزع وتحير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon loses its light.
rows.anchor: أي ذهب ضوء القمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon are brought together in losing their light.
rows.anchor: أي جمعا في ذهاب نورهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is read with fatḥa or kasra on fāʾ: fatḥa means escape, while kasra means the place of escape.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ (أين المفر) - بكسر الفاء - فمن فتح فهو بمعنى أين الفرار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pattern mafʿal with fatḥa can mark a verbal noun, as in jalasa majlisan meaning sitting; the same form with kasra marks a place, as in where one sat.
rows.anchor: والمفعل من مثل جلست بفتح العين، وكذلك المصدر، تقول: جلست مجلسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wazar originally means a mountain people take refuge in; by extension it means anything one seeks as shelter or escape.
rows.anchor: الوزر في كلام العرب الجبل الذي يلجأ إليه: هذا أصله، وكل ما التجأت إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There will be no fortress or place of escape for them.
rows.anchor: ثم أعلم تعالى أنه لا حرز لهم ولا محيص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person is a witness against himself because his own limbs will testify to what he did, as other Qur'anic passages state explicitly.
rows.anchor: معناه بل الإنسان تشهد عليه جوارحه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that a person could present every argument or excuse he has.
rows.anchor: ولو أدلى بكل حجة عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An exegetical report glosses maʿādhīr as curtains, with singular miʿdhār.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير المعاذير الستور، واحدها معذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Gabriel brought revelation, the Prophet repeated it aloud for fear it might slip away; God reassured him that He would gather and preserve it in his heart.
rows.anchor: كان جبريل عليه السلام إذا نزل بالوحي على النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God undertakes to teach the Prophet the revelation so he will not forget it and to recite it to him.
rows.anchor: أي إن عليناأن نقرئك فلا تنسى، وعلينا تلاوته عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told not to hurry in reciting until the revelation for its proper time has been recited to him.
rows.anchor: أي لا تعجل بالتلاوة إلى أن تقرأ عليك ما ينزل في وقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God undertakes to send it down as clear Arabic without crookedness, containing an explanation for people.
rows.anchor: أي علينا أن ننزله قرآنا عربيا غير ذي عوج، فيه بيان للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person described is Abū Jahl ibn Hishām.
rows.anchor: يعنى به أبو جهل بن هشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An exegetical saying declares that every community has a Pharaoh and that Abū Jahl ibn Hishām was this community's Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير إن لكل أمة فرعونا، وإن فرعون هذه الأمة أبو جهل بن هشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatamaṭṭā means strutting, derived from maṭā, the back.
rows.anchor: معناه بتبختر، مأخوذ من المطا وهو الظهر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that harm is close to you, Abū Jahl; Arabs use awlā for someone as a curse invoking harm.
rows.anchor: معناه - والله أعلم - وليك المكروه يا أبا جهل، والعرب تقول أولى لفلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To be left sudan means to be left without commands or prohibitions.
rows.anchor: أي أن يترك غير مأمور وغير منهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjāj moves from rejecting an aimless life to demonstrating Resurrection through God's power to initiate creation.
rows.anchor: (ألم يك نطفة من مني يمنى (37)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is read tumna, agreeing with feminine nuṭfa, or yumnā, agreeing with masculine maniyy.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأ (تمنى) فللفظ النطفة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recalling creation from a drop, the passage asks whether the one who formed the sexes is not capable of bringing the dead to life.
rows.anchor: (أليس ذلك بقادر على أن يحيي الموتى (40)
